This document lists the R packages explicitly referenced in the Workshop 1
source materials. It is intended as a planning aid for checking installation
requirements across all modules, not only Module 5.

## Scope

Source scanned:

- `materials/1-workshop1/**/*.qmd`
- `materials/1-workshop1/**/*.Qmd`
- `materials/1-workshop1/**/*.R`

Reference point:

- Upstream branch: `origin/main`
- Upstream commit scanned: `d0e1724`

Detection rules:

- Included direct `library()` and `require()` calls.
- Included explicit namespace calls such as `pkg::function()`.
- Included explicit `install.packages("pkg")` calls.
- Included tidyverse member packages when their functions appear in course
  materials, even if the file loads them through `library(tidyverse)`.
- Excluded transitive dependencies that only appear in `renv.lock`.
- Excluded Quarto, Pandoc, and browser-side JavaScript/CSS dependencies.

## Tidyverse Note

`tidyverse` is a meta-package. Loading it also loads the core packages commonly
used throughout the course, including `ggplot2`, `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `readr`,
`purrr`, `tibble`, `stringr`, and `forcats`.

Because the course often uses `library(tidyverse)`, individual tidyverse member
packages may be used without appearing separately as `library(ggplot2)` or
`library(dplyr)` in every file.

The interactive cheatsheet surfaces the member packages that learners actually
meet through function names, so `ggplot2`, `readr`, `tidyr`, `forcats`,
`tibble`, and `stringr` are not hidden under the `tidyverse` umbrella.

## Items To Review

- `survival` is still detected in Module 5 `notes.qmd`, even though the updated
  Exercise 1 no longer asks about survival models.
- `purrr` appears in Module 5 helper code. It is listed for transparency, but
  can remain outside the main participant learning path unless iteration is
  added as a teaching topic.
- `MASS`, `lme4`, `lmerTest`, and `broom.mixed` are modeling-specific packages
  that may need extra attention during setup checks.
- `countdown` is used broadly in slides, so slide rendering can fail even when
  the analysis packages are installed correctly.
